symptoms: Long (3–15 cm), cigar-shaped grey-green to tan lesions on leaves
Lesions start on lower leaves and move up; dark spores can appear in the centre in humid weather
Severe infection before tasselling dries leaves early and reduces yield
diseases.spread: Survives on maize residue; spores spread by wind and rain splash. Favoured by moderate temperatures (18–27 °C), heavy dew and long wet periods.
cultural: Plant resistant or tolerant varieties recommended for your area
Rotate with a non-grass crop (beans, soybean, groundnut) for at least one season
Bury or remove infected residue after harvest
Avoid very dense planting so leaves dry faster
biological: Trichoderma-based products can reduce inoculum on residue (moderate effect)
chemical: Only if lesions reach the ear leaf before or at tasselling on a susceptible variety
Triazoles (e.g. propiconazole, tebuconazole) or strobilurin + triazole mixtures
diseases.prevention: Resistant varieties and rotation give the best long-term control.

symptoms: Narrow, rectangular grey to tan lesions limited by leaf veins
Lesions join and kill large leaf areas during grain fill
diseases.spread: Survives on residue; favoured by warm, very humid weather, mist and reduced tillage. Common in East and Southern African highlands.
cultural: Use tolerant hybrids
Rotate away from maize and manage residue
Avoid continuous maize under minimum tillage in high-risk zones
biological: No reliable biocontrol yet; focus on resistance and rotation
chemical: Strobilurin or strobilurin + triazole fungicides at early lesion development on susceptible varieties
diseases.prevention: Choose tolerant varieties for humid, high-altitude areas.

symptoms: Small, oval, cinnamon-brown powdery pustules on both leaf surfaces
Pustules turn dark brown-black late in the season
diseases.spread: Wind-blown spores; favoured by cool (16–23 °C), humid conditions.
cultural: Plant resistant hybrids; most commercial hybrids have good tolerance
Plant early to avoid peak spore periods
chemical: Usually not needed. On susceptible seed crops, triazole or strobilurin fungicides at early infection

diseases.scientific: Maize streak virus (Mastrevirus), spread by Cicadulina leafhoppers
symptoms: Narrow, broken yellow-white streaks running along the leaf veins
Plants infected young are stunted and may produce no cobs
diseases.spread: Transmitted only by Cicadulina leafhoppers from grasses and earlier maize. Worst in late-planted fields and dry spells. Native to Africa.
cultural: Plant MSV-resistant varieties (widely available in Africa)
Plant early and at the same time as neighbours
Remove infected seedlings early and control grass weeds around the field
biological: Natural enemies of leafhoppers; avoid broad-spectrum insecticides that kill them
chemical: No chemical cure for the virus
Systemic insecticide seed treatment (e.g. imidacloprid, thiamethoxam) can reduce early leafhopper feeding in high-risk areas
diseases.prevention: Resistant varieties plus synchronized early planting.

diseases.scientific: Maize chlorotic mottle virus + a potyvirus (usually SCMV)
symptoms: Yellow mottling starting at leaf bases, then drying from the leaf margins inward ("firing")
Dead heart, premature drying, small or empty cobs; whole fields can die
diseases.spread: Thrips, rootworms and aphids spread the viruses; MCMV is also seed-borne. Spread rapidly in East Africa since 2011.
cultural: Use certified MLN-free seed and MLN-tolerant varieties
Do not plant maize continuously; observe maize-free periods where advised
Uproot and destroy infected plants early; control weeds
Rotate with legumes, potato or other non-cereals
biological: No biocontrol for the virus; conserve vector enemies
chemical: No chemical cure
Vector control (seed treatment, insecticides against thrips/aphids) only as advised by extension
diseases.prevention: Certified seed, rotation and community-wide maize-free periods.
diseases.notes: Notifiable in several countries. Report suspected MLN to your extension or plant-protection office.

symptoms: Window-pane feeding (scraped, see-through patches) on young leaves
Ragged holes, sawdust-like droppings (frass) in the leaf funnel (whorl)
Caterpillars with an inverted "Y" on the head and four dots in a square near the tail
diseases.spread: Moths fly long distances; spread across Africa since 2016. Several generations per season.
cultural: Scout twice a week in the first 6 weeks; act early
Hand-pick egg masses and young larvae; put sand, ash or soil mixed with lime in the whorl
Plant early and at the same time; intercrop with legumes; "push-pull" with desmodium and Brachiaria
biological: Products based on Bt (Bacillus thuringiensis), Metarhizium or SfMNPV virus
Protect natural enemies (parasitic wasps, earwigs, ants)
chemical: Only if damage exceeds local thresholds (about 20% of young plants damaged)
Use recommended actives such as emamectin benzoate, spinetoram or chlorantraniliprole; spray into the whorl; rotate modes of action
diseases.prevention: Regular scouting, push-pull, early synchronized planting.

symptoms: Elongated, dark reddish-brown pustules on stems, leaf sheaths and leaves that tear the plant skin
Pustules turn black late in the season; stems weaken and lodge
diseases.spread: Wind-blown spores over long distances; warm days (20–30 °C) with wet nights. Ug99 races arose in East Africa.
cultural: Grow resistant varieties released for your country (check for Ug99 resistance)
Remove volunteer wheat and avoid very late planting
chemical: Triazoles (e.g. tebuconazole, propiconazole) or triazole + strobilurin at first sign on susceptible varieties
diseases.prevention: Resistant varieties; surveillance with extension services.
diseases.notes: Report new outbreaks to extension; Ug99-lineage races threaten many varieties.

symptoms: Small, round, orange-brown pustules scattered on the upper leaf surface
diseases.spread: Wind-blown spores; mild temperatures (15–22 °C) and dew.
cultural: Resistant varieties; remove volunteer wheat; avoid excess nitrogen
chemical: Triazole fungicides when pustules appear on upper leaves before flowering

symptoms: Yellow-orange pustules in long stripes between the leaf veins
Leaves turn yellow and dry; heads can be infected
diseases.spread: Cool (10–15 °C), moist weather; a major problem in the Ethiopian and Kenyan highlands.
cultural: Resistant varieties; avoid early sowing in hot-spot areas; remove volunteers
chemical: Triazoles (e.g. tebuconazole, propiconazole) at first stripes on susceptible varieties
diseases.prevention: Resistant varieties and early scouting in cool, wet seasons.

symptoms: Brown, irregular blotches with tiny black dots (fruiting bodies) inside
Starts on lower leaves and moves up in rain
diseases.spread: Rain splash from residue; cool, wet seasons.
cultural: Rotation, residue management, tolerant varieties, avoid very early sowing
chemical: Triazole or SDHI-containing mixtures at flag-leaf stage on susceptible varieties

symptoms: White to grey fluffy patches on leaves and stems that rub off
diseases.spread: Wind; dense crops, high humidity and high nitrogen.
cultural: Resistant varieties; balanced nitrogen; avoid very dense sowing
biological: Sulphur products are accepted in organic systems
chemical: Sulphur or triazole fungicides if more than a few upper leaves are covered before flowering

symptoms: Diamond-shaped lesions with grey centres and brown edges on leaves
Neck blast: the stem below the panicle turns black and the panicle breaks or stays empty
diseases.spread: Airborne spores; long leaf wetness, cool nights, high nitrogen. Major threat in upland rice in Africa.
cultural: Resistant varieties; split nitrogen applications; avoid excess nitrogen
Keep fields flooded where possible; destroy infected straw
biological: Silicon fertilisers and Pseudomonas / Bacillus seed treatments reduce severity
chemical: Tricyclazole, azoxystrobin or isoprothiolane at booting if blast is present

symptoms: Oval brown spots with a grey centre and yellow halo on leaves and grains
diseases.spread: Seed-borne; worst on poor, nutrient-deficient soils and in drought stress.
cultural: Use clean seed; correct potassium, silicon and nitrogen deficiencies
chemical: Seed treatment with a recommended fungicide; foliar triazole in severe cases
diseases.prevention: Healthy soil fertility and clean seed.

symptoms: Wavy yellow to white stripes starting at leaf tips or edges, drying to grey
Milky bacterial ooze drops in the morning
diseases.spread: Water, wind-driven rain, wounds, infected stubble; warm and flooded conditions.
cultural: Resistant varieties; balanced nitrogen; drain fields periodically; clean tools; remove stubble
chemical: Copper products have limited value; resistance and hygiene are the real control

symptoms: Narrow, water-soaked streaks between veins that turn yellow-brown, with amber droplets
diseases.spread: Rain splash, wind, irrigation water and seed.
cultural: Clean seed, resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen, remove infected stubble
chemical: Copper products have limited value

symptoms: Grains discoloured straw to grey with a brown base; panicles stay upright because grains are empty
diseases.spread: Seed-borne; very hot nights during flowering.
cultural: Clean seed; avoid planting so that flowering falls in the hottest period; moderate nitrogen
chemical: No effective chemical control in most countries

diseases.scientific: Rice tungro bacilliform + spherical viruses (green leafhoppers)
symptoms: Yellow-orange leaves from the tip down, stunting, fewer tillers
diseases.spread: Green leafhoppers.
cultural: Resistant varieties; synchronised planting; remove infected stubble and volunteers
chemical: No chemical cure; insecticides against leafhoppers only on extension advice

symptoms: White parallel feeding streaks and blotch mines on leaves; small spiny dark beetles
diseases.spread: Adult beetles fly between fields; favoured by excess nitrogen and heavy rain.
cultural: Clip and destroy leaf tips with eggs before transplanting; avoid excess nitrogen
chemical: Only at high infestations, using recommended insecticides

diseases.scientific: Rice stem borers (e.g. Scirpophaga, Chilo, Maliarpha spp.)
symptoms: Central shoot dries and pulls out easily at the vegetative stage; white empty heads later
diseases.spread: Moths lay eggs on leaves; larvae bore into stems.
cultural: Harvest close to the ground and destroy stubble; synchronised planting; remove egg masses
biological: Trichogramma egg parasitoids; conserve natural enemies
chemical: Only if above local thresholds; use recommended insecticides

symptoms: Twisted, thickened yellowish leaves; stunted plants; distorted panicles
diseases.spread: Waterlogged or flooded seedlings in cool weather.
cultural: Good drainage at seedling stage; remove infected plants; control grassy weeds
chemical: Rarely justified
diseases.prevention: Good water management at seedling stage.

symptoms: Small round to elliptical spots with tan or red centres and dark margins; black spore dots in the centre
Stalk rot and red discoloration inside stems in severe cases
diseases.spread: Residue, seed, rain splash; warm, humid weather.
cultural: Resistant varieties, rotation, residue removal, clean seed
chemical: Seed treatment; foliar triazole or strobilurin only on susceptible varieties in high pressure

symptoms: Long, elliptical reddish or tan lesions on leaves
diseases.spread: Residue and wind-blown spores; humid, moderate temperatures.
cultural: Resistant varieties, rotation, residue management
chemical: Rarely economic; triazoles on seed crops

symptoms: Small reddish-brown to purple pustules on both leaf surfaces
diseases.spread: Wind-blown spores.
cultural: Resistant varieties; early planting
chemical: Rarely needed

symptoms: Small reddish-brown streaks parallel to leaf veins that become black spots with grey centres
Large dead leaf areas; bunches ripen early and are small
diseases.spread: Wind and rain; warm, wet weather.
cultural: Cut and remove (de-leaf) infected leaves and leaf parts every 1–2 weeks
Good drainage, correct spacing, weed control; tolerant varieties
chemical: Mineral oil plus protectants (mancozeb, chlorothalonil) or systemics (triazoles, strobilurins) in commercial plantations; rotate groups

diseases.scientific: Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense (incl. Tropical Race 4)
symptoms: Older leaves turn yellow from the edges and collapse around the stem like a skirt
Splitting of the pseudostem base; reddish-brown streaks inside when cut
diseases.spread: Soil, infected suckers, water, tools, shoes and vehicles. Survives decades in soil.
cultural: Plant clean tissue-culture plantlets of resistant varieties
Do not move soil, suckers or tools from infected fields; disinfect boots and tools
Destroy infected plants on the spot; do not replant bananas there
biological: Soil health and Trichoderma may reduce disease; no cure
chemical: No effective chemical cure
diseases.prevention: Quarantine, clean planting material, resistant varieties.
diseases.notes: Tropical Race 4 is a quarantine pest. Report suspected cases to the plant-protection service.

symptoms: Yellowing and wilting leaves; fruits ripen early and unevenly with brown stains inside; male bud shrivels
Yellow bacterial ooze from cut stems
diseases.spread: Insects visiting the male flower, contaminated tools, infected suckers. Major threat in East and Central Africa.
cultural: Remove the male bud with a forked stick as soon as the last hand forms
Disinfect tools (fire or bleach) between plants; use clean suckers
Cut down and bury infected plants (single diseased stem removal)
chemical: No chemical cure; bleach for tool disinfection only
diseases.notes: Report new outbreaks to extension; community action is needed.

symptoms: Dark irregular spots on leaves, blackened flowers, dark sunken spots on fruit that grow during ripening
diseases.spread: Rain and dew during flowering and fruit set.
cultural: Prune for airflow; remove dead twigs and fallen leaves; harvest carefully
biological: Bacillus-based products; hot-water dip of fruit (52–55 °C for 5 minutes) after harvest
chemical: Copper, mancozeb or azoxystrobin during flowering and fruit set in wet weather

symptoms: Raised black, angular spots with a yellow halo on leaves; cracked black spots on fruit
diseases.spread: Wind-driven rain, wounds, infected planting material.
cultural: Windbreaks; prune and burn infected twigs; disinfect tools; clean planting material
chemical: Copper sprays after pruning and before rainy periods

symptoms: White powder on young leaves, flowers and young fruit; flowers drop
diseases.spread: Wind; cool nights and dry days during flowering.
cultural: Prune for airflow; remove infected panicles
chemical: Sulphur or triazoles at flowering

diseases.scientific: Capnodium spp. (grows on honeydew from insects)
symptoms: Black, soot-like coating on leaves that can be rubbed off
diseases.spread: Grows on honeydew from scales, mealybugs, aphids and hoppers.
cultural: Control the sap-sucking insects; prune for light and airflow
biological: Conserve ladybirds and parasitoids; soap or oil sprays against the insects
chemical: Treat the insects, not the mould

symptoms: Twigs dry from the tip backwards; leaves turn brown and stay attached; gum on branches
diseases.spread: Wounds, stress and infected wood.
cultural: Cut 10 cm below the dead part into healthy wood and burn cuttings; seal large cuts
chemical: Copper paste or spray after pruning
diseases.prevention: Good tree nutrition and pruning hygiene.

symptoms: Small raised warty galls on leaves; damaged flowers and young fruit
diseases.spread: Flying midges; larvae drop to the soil to pupate.
cultural: Remove and destroy galled leaves; plough soil under trees to expose pupae
chemical: Only on advice at flushing / flowering

symptoms: Young leaves cut off neatly near the base, as if with scissors
diseases.spread: Adult weevils lay eggs in tender leaves.
cultural: Collect and destroy fallen cut leaves
chemical: Only at heavy infestation during new flushes

symptoms: Blotchy yellow mottling that is not the same on both halves of the leaf; small, lopsided, bitter fruit that stays green
diseases.spread: Psyllids (African citrus psyllid Trioza erytreae; Asian Diaphorina citri) and infected budwood.
cultural: Plant certified disease-free seedlings; remove infected trees; control psyllids area-wide
chemical: No cure; psyllid control on extension advice
diseases.prevention: Clean nursery stock and psyllid management.
diseases.notes: Report suspected HLB; it is a quarantine disease in many countries.

symptoms: Raised, corky brown spots with a yellow halo on leaves, twigs and fruit
diseases.spread: Wind-driven rain, leaf miners, contaminated tools.
cultural: Windbreaks; prune infected twigs; control leaf miner; disinfect tools
chemical: Copper sprays on new flushes and young fruit

symptoms: Hard, sunken spots with brown edges and grey centres on fruit; small spots on leaves
diseases.spread: Leaf litter and rain during fruit development.
cultural: Remove leaf litter; prune
chemical: Copper or strobilurins during the susceptible fruit period

symptoms: Small, raised, rough dark brown dots on leaves and fruit, like sandpaper
diseases.spread: Dead twigs in the tree; rain.
cultural: Prune out dead wood
chemical: Copper after petal fall in wet regions

symptoms: Olive-green to black velvety spots on leaves and fruit; fruit cracks
diseases.spread: Fallen leaves; spring rains.
cultural: Rake and destroy fallen leaves; prune for airflow; resistant varieties
chemical: Captan, dithiocarbamates or triazoles during wet spring periods

symptoms: Leaf spots with purple edges and tan centres ("frog-eye"); fruit rot with rings; cankers on limbs
diseases.spread: Dead wood, mummified fruit; warm, wet weather.
cultural: Remove mummified fruit and dead wood; prune out cankers
chemical: Captan or strobilurins in the season

symptoms: Bright yellow-orange spots on leaves, later with small tubes underneath
diseases.spread: Alternates between juniper (cedar) and apple.
cultural: Resistant varieties; remove nearby junipers where practical
chemical: Triazoles (e.g. myclobutanil) in spring

symptoms: White powdery coating on young leaves and shoots
diseases.spread: Infected buds; dry warm days, humid nights.
cultural: Prune out infected shoots
chemical: Sulphur or triazoles
diseases.prevention: Remove infected shoots in winter pruning.

symptoms: Tan leaf spots with dark borders and black dots; berries shrivel into hard black mummies
diseases.spread: Mummies and canes; warm, wet weather.
cultural: Remove mummies and infected canes; open canopy
chemical: Mancozeb, captan or triazoles from early shoot growth to berry set

diseases.scientific: Phaeomoniella chlamydospora and other trunk fungi
symptoms: Tiger-stripe leaves: yellow or red between veins with dry centres; dark spots on berries; sudden vine collapse
diseases.spread: Pruning wounds.
cultural: Prune in dry weather; protect large cuts; remove dead vines
chemical: No curative treatment

symptoms: Dark red-brown irregular spots on leaves; early leaf drop
diseases.spread: Warm, humid weather.
cultural: Open canopy; remove infected leaves
chemical: Mancozeb or copper if severe

symptoms: Small angular dark spots that fall out ("shot holes"); cracked spots on fruit
diseases.spread: Wind-driven rain; sandy soils.
cultural: Resistant varieties; windbreaks; balanced nitrogen
chemical: Copper at leaf fall and early spring; oxytetracycline where registered

symptoms: White powdery patches on young leaves; leaves curl
diseases.spread: Wind; warm days and humid nights.
cultural: Prune for airflow; remove root suckers
chemical: Sulphur or triazoles

symptoms: Many small purple spots that merge; leaves look burnt
diseases.spread: Infected plants and rain splash.
cultural: Clean planting material; remove old leaves after harvest; drip irrigation
chemical: Captan or triazoles if severe

symptoms: Yellow-orange powdery spots on the underside of leaves; pale yellow patches on top
Heavy leaf fall and branch die-back
diseases.spread: Wind and rain splash; warm, humid weather; more severe at lower altitudes and on heavily bearing trees.
cultural: Resistant varieties; shade management; balanced nutrition; prune for airflow
chemical: Copper-based protectants before the rainy season; triazoles (e.g. cyproconazole) where registered
diseases.prevention: Resistant varieties and good farm management.

symptoms: Round brown spots with a light grey centre and yellow halo ("eye"); spots on berries
diseases.spread: Wind and splash; stressed, under-fertilised, unshaded trees.
cultural: Shade; balanced nutrition (especially nitrogen and potassium); weed control
chemical: Copper-based fungicides

symptoms: Dark brown irregular spots, often at the leaf edges and tips; die-back of young shoots
diseases.spread: Cold winds and high altitude; wounds.
cultural: Windbreaks; avoid cold, exposed sites
chemical: Copper or strobilurins on advice

symptoms: Irregular brown blotch mines on the upper leaf surface; leaves drop
diseases.spread: Moths; dry seasons.
cultural: Shade and windbreaks; avoid excessive insecticides
chemical: Only if thresholds are exceeded, using recommended insecticides

symptoms: Upper leaf surface turns dull bronze-brown; fine webbing
diseases.spread: Dry weather and dust.
cultural: Shade; reduce dust; avoid broad-spectrum insecticides
chemical: Specific acaricides only if severe

symptoms: Angular brown or grey spots bounded by leaf veins, often with a yellow edge
Spots join; leaves drop early; brown spots on pods
diseases.spread: Seed and crop residue; rain splash and wind; warm, humid weather. One of the most damaging bean diseases in Africa.
cultural: Plant clean (certified) seed of resistant varieties
Rotate for at least two seasons; bury or remove residue
Avoid working in the field when leaves are wet
biological: Trichoderma or Bacillus seed treatment gives partial protection
chemical: Seed treatment; foliar mancozeb, chlorothalonil, or triazole sprays at first symptoms on susceptible varieties

symptoms: Small reddish-brown powdery pustules, often with a yellow halo, mostly on the leaf underside
diseases.spread: Wind-blown spores; long dew periods at 17–27 °C.
cultural: Resistant varieties; rotation; destroy volunteer beans and residue
chemical: Triazoles (e.g. tebuconazole) or mancozeb at first pustules

symptoms: Round brown spots with a clear yellow halo, mainly on the upper leaf surface
diseases.spread: Residue, rain splash; warm, humid weather.
cultural: Rotate 2–3 years away from groundnut; bury residue; resistant varieties; remove volunteers
biological: Trichoderma and neem-based sprays give partial control
chemical: Chlorothalonil, mancozeb or triazoles (e.g. tebuconazole) from 30–35 days after sowing in high-risk areas

symptoms: Dark brown to black round spots, usually without a strong halo; dark tufts on the leaf underside
Heavy defoliation before harvest
diseases.spread: Residue and wind; warm, wet weather late in the season.
cultural: Rotation; residue burial; resistant varieties; timely harvest
chemical: Chlorothalonil, mancozeb or triazoles as for early leaf spot

symptoms: Orange-brown pustules on the leaf underside that burst and release powdery spores
diseases.spread: Wind; high humidity.
cultural: Resistant varieties; remove volunteers; early sowing
chemical: Triazoles or chlorothalonil at first pustules

diseases.scientific: Groundnut rosette disease complex (spread by Aphis craccivora)
symptoms: Stunted, bushy plants with small, curled, yellow (chlorotic) or dark green mottled leaves
diseases.spread: Aphids; worst in late-sown, sparse stands. Unique to Africa.
cultural: Resistant varieties; early sowing; dense, uniform plant stands; uproot early infected plants
chemical: No cure; aphid control only on extension advice
diseases.prevention: Early dense sowing with resistant varieties.

symptoms: Yellow or pale green mosaic on leaves; leaves distorted, twisted and smaller
Stunted plants with low root yield
diseases.spread: Infected stem cuttings (main source) and whiteflies.
cultural: Plant cuttings only from healthy, symptom-free plants
Use CMD-resistant varieties
Uproot and destroy infected plants early (roguing)
chemical: No chemical cure; whitefly sprays are rarely effective
diseases.prevention: Clean planting material and resistant varieties.

diseases.scientific: Cassava brown streak ipomoviruses (whitefly Bemisia tabaci)
symptoms: Yellow patches along secondary veins of older leaves; brown streaks on green stems
Dry, brown, corky rot inside the roots; roots unsellable
diseases.spread: Infected cuttings and whiteflies. Spreading across East and Central Africa.
cultural: Use certified clean cuttings of tolerant varieties
Rogue infected plants; harvest early in affected areas
chemical: No chemical cure
diseases.prevention: Clean seed systems and tolerant varieties.
diseases.notes: Report new areas of CBSD to your extension office.

diseases.scientific: Xanthomonas axonopodis pv. manihotis (X. phaseoli pv. manihotis)
symptoms: Angular water-soaked spots, leaf wilting and blight, gum on stems, shoot die-back
diseases.spread: Infected cuttings, rain splash, tools; rainy season.
cultural: Clean cuttings from healthy plants; resistant varieties; rotation; disinfect tools; remove infected plants
chemical: No effective chemical control in the field

diseases.scientific: Cassava green mottle virus (also used for green mite-like mottling in datasets)
symptoms: Small yellow-green mottled spots, leaf distortion; often confused with green mite damage
diseases.spread: Infected cuttings.
cultural: Healthy cuttings; remove affected plants
biological: For green mite: predatory mites (Typhlodromalus aripo) released in many African countries
chemical: No chemical cure for the virus

symptoms: Dark, water-soaked patches on leaves that spread fast; white mould at the edge underneath in humid weather
Brown, rotting stems; reddish-brown dry rot in tubers
diseases.spread: Infected tubers and volunteers; airborne spores; cool (10–24 °C), wet weather. Can destroy a field in a week.
cultural: Plant certified healthy seed tubers of resistant varieties
Destroy volunteer potatoes and cull piles; hill up soil over tubers
Remove and bury infected plants; cut haulms 2 weeks before harvest
biological: Bacillus subtilis products give weak protection; not enough alone
chemical: Protectant sprays (mancozeb, chlorothalonil, copper) before infection in wet weather
Systemics (metalaxyl-M + mancozeb, cymoxanil, dimethomorph) once disease is present; rotate groups
diseases.prevention: Resistant varieties, healthy seed and a spray plan in rainy seasons.

symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings ("target board") on older leaves, often with a yellow halo
diseases.spread: Residue and soil; warm weather with alternating wet and dry periods; stressed plants.
cultural: Rotation; balanced fertilisation; avoid drought stress; remove residue
biological: Bacillus or Trichoderma products give partial control
chemical: Mancozeb, chlorothalonil, or strobilurins / difenoconazole when spots appear on lower leaves

diseases.scientific: Ralstonia solanacearum, Pectobacterium spp. and others

symptoms: Sudden wilting of green plants; brown ring in the cut tuber with white ooze (bacterial wilt)
Black, slimy stem base and soft, smelly tubers (blackleg / soft rot)
diseases.spread: Infected seed tubers, soil, water, tools. Bacterial wilt is a major problem in African highlands.
cultural: Certified clean seed; rotate 3+ years with cereals; uproot infected plants with the soil around them
Clean tools; avoid irrigation water from infected fields
chemical: No effective chemical control

symptoms: Mosaic, mottling, rolled or crinkled leaves, stunted plants
diseases.spread: Aphids and infected seed tubers.
cultural: Certified seed; rogue infected plants early; control volunteers and weeds
chemical: No cure; mineral oil or aphicides only in seed production

diseases.scientific: e.g. potato tuber moth, aphids, leaf miners
symptoms: Holes, mines or chewed leaves; insects or larvae visible
diseases.spread: Varies by pest.
cultural: Hill up soil to protect tubers; remove infested plants; store tubers covered and cool
biological: Granulovirus or Bt products for tuber moth; conserve natural enemies
chemical: Only if thresholds are exceeded; use recommended insecticides

symptoms: Patches of stunted, yellowing plants; galls on roots or tiny cysts on roots
diseases.spread: Soil, infected tubers, tools and water.
cultural: Long rotation with non-host crops; clean seed; resistant varieties where available
biological: Organic amendments and biofumigation (brassicas) reduce populations
chemical: Nematicides only under expert guidance

symptoms: Large, greasy grey-green to brown patches on leaves; white mould underneath in humid weather
Brown streaks on stems; firm brown blotches on fruit
diseases.spread: Airborne spores from infected potato or tomato; cool, wet weather. Very fast.
cultural: Do not plant next to potatoes; use resistant varieties; stake and prune for airflow
Water at the base, not on leaves; remove and bury infected plants immediately
biological: Bacillus-based products give weak protection only
chemical: Protectants (mancozeb, chlorothalonil, copper) before rainy spells
Systemics (metalaxyl-M + mancozeb, cymoxanil, dimethomorph) after first symptoms; rotate groups
diseases.prevention: Resistant varieties and a preventive spray plan in the wet season.

symptoms: Brown spots with concentric rings on older leaves, yellowing around spots
Dark sunken spots near the stem end of fruit
diseases.spread: Soil and residue; rain splash; warm, humid weather.
cultural: Rotate 2–3 years away from tomato, potato, pepper and eggplant
Mulch, stake, remove lower leaves touching soil, water at the base
chemical: Mancozeb, chlorothalonil, copper, or difenoconazole / azoxystrobin at first spots

symptoms: Small, dark, greasy spots on leaves, sometimes with a yellow halo; scabby spots on fruit
diseases.spread: Seed, transplants, rain splash and handling wet plants.
cultural: Clean seed and transplants; avoid overhead irrigation; do not work in wet plants; rotation
chemical: Copper products (often mixed with mancozeb) as protection; resistance to copper is common

symptoms: Pale yellow patches on the upper leaf surface; olive-green to brown velvety mould underneath
diseases.spread: Very high humidity (over 85%), especially in greenhouses and tunnels.
cultural: Ventilate greenhouses; reduce humidity; prune for airflow; resistant varieties
chemical: Chlorothalonil, mancozeb or difenoconazole if needed

symptoms: Many small round spots with a grey-white centre and dark border on lower leaves; tiny black dots inside
diseases.spread: Residue and weeds; rain splash; warm, wet weather.
cultural: Rotation; remove lower infected leaves; mulch; control nightshade weeds
chemical: Chlorothalonil, mancozeb or copper at first spots

symptoms: Fine yellow speckling on leaves, bronzing, fine webbing on the underside
diseases.spread: Hot, dry, dusty conditions; overuse of broad-spectrum insecticides.
cultural: Avoid drought stress; spray water under leaves; remove heavily infested leaves
biological: Predatory mites (Phytoseiulus); neem oil; insecticidal soap
chemical: Specific acaricides (e.g. abamectin, spiromesifen); rotate actives; avoid pyrethroids that worsen outbreaks

symptoms: Brown spots with light rings that can merge; spots on fruit near the stem
diseases.spread: Residue; warm, humid weather.
cultural: Rotation; pruning for airflow; remove residue
chemical: Chlorothalonil, mancozeb, or azoxystrobin / difenoconazole

symptoms: Small, upward-curled leaves with yellow edges; stunted, bushy plants; few fruits
diseases.spread: Whiteflies.
cultural: Resistant varieties; insect-proof nurseries; remove infected plants early; yellow sticky traps; control weeds
chemical: No cure; whitefly control in nurseries and early growth only on advice
diseases.prevention: Clean, protected seedlings and resistant varieties.

diseases.scientific: Tomato mosaic virus / Tobacco mosaic virus (Tobamovirus)
symptoms: Light and dark green mosaic, fern-like or distorted leaves, uneven fruit ripening
diseases.spread: Contact: hands, tools, clothing, tobacco products, seed.
cultural: Wash hands and tools; do not smoke while handling plants; remove infected plants; resistant varieties
chemical: No cure

symptoms: Small water-soaked spots turning brown; yellow leaves drop; raised scabby spots on fruit
diseases.spread: Seed, transplants, rain splash.
cultural: Clean seed and transplants; rotation; avoid overhead watering
chemical: Copper (often with mancozeb) as protection

symptoms: White powdery patches on leaves and stems; leaves yellow and dry
diseases.spread: Wind; warm days and cool nights; does not need rain.
cultural: Resistant varieties; good spacing; remove old infected leaves
biological: Sulphur, potassium bicarbonate, milk sprays (1 part milk : 9 parts water) or Bacillus products
chemical: Sulphur, or triazoles / strobilurins at first patches; rotate groups
